**Claim.** Valloud argues that *[[Laws of Form]]* plausibly influenced Smalltalk’s conceptual framing: “distinctions”, “forms”, and the idea that naming is an *act* that changes what is available to thought and computation. 

**Why it matters (course context).** This appendix is not “history trivia”; it is a design lens: treat Smalltalk as a machine for **drawing distinctions cheaply**, then **naming** them so behavior can be mounted and recombined.
See [[A Mentoring Course on Smalltalk]] – Appendix A — [[Design distinctions behind Smalltalk]] and [[Design Principles Behind Smalltalk]]
